subtopic: Loop-level IR: affine analysis and loop reordering
learningObjective: Reason about when two nested loops in a loop-level IR can be safely interchanged based on the affine access patterns of the loop body.
stem: Consider the loop nest below (loop-level IR). The pass wants to interchange the `i` and `j` loops. Which condition is required for the swap to preserve semantics?

options.text: Interchange preserves semantics iff no dependence in the original loop nest is violated by the reordering — for pure elementwise stores that read and write disjoint per-iteration locations (no loop-carried dependence), interchange is safe.
The swap is always safe because loop bounds are constant integers and the loop body is purely elementwise; interchange is a syntactic transformation that never changes semantics.

Interchange is unsafe here because `M` and `N` may differ; only square loop nests (`M == N`) can be interchanged, so a runtime check is required. In this description, only square loop nests where the loop bounds are equal integer constants can be interchanged safely; rectangular nests such as `M != N` require a preliminary padding pass to align the iteration domains before the swap.

Interchange requires the compiler to first fully unroll one of the loops; loop interchange on rolled loops is not a supported transformation in affine IR. Under this account, interchange in an affine IR must be preceded by fully unrolling the outer loop into straight-line code; the interchange transformation is defined only on unrolled loop bodies where the induction variable has been specialized to concrete values.

explanation: Loop interchange preserves semantics iff every dependence direction vector in the original nest remains legal after the swap. For an elementwise nest that reads B[i,j] and writes C[i,j] with disjoint iterations (no loop-carried dependence), any permutation of loops is safe. In general, dependence-vector analysis is required: a dependence with a `< , >` direction pair becomes `> , <` after interchange, which is illegal. Loop bounds and shape equalities are irrelevant to legality; unrolling is not a prerequisite.

optionExplanations.B: Wrong: interchange is not always safe; loop-carried dependences can be violated.
optionExplanations.A: Correct: standard dependence-based legality rule for loop interchange.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: legality does not depend on equality of the loop trip counts.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: interchange operates on rolled loops directly.

assumptions: The IR is affine (indices are affine functions of loop induction variables) so dependence analysis is tractable.
The two loops iterate independently within their bounds.
nonImplications: Does not imply that legal interchange always improves performance; cache access pattern matters.
Does not imply interchange is the only reordering: skewing and tiling are related but distinct.
